entities.name: PMID:25433272
observations: In cultured rat patellar-tendon-derived tenocytes, triamcinolone acetonide and lidocaine alone reduced viability and altered morphology; the combination with 1% lidocaine caused significantly lower viability and more pronounced morphological changes than either agent alone, described by the authors as synergistic potentiation.

entities.name: PMID:30035090
observations: In canine supraspinatus tendon explants, 1% lidocaine reduced tenocyte viability and tissue metabolism at days 1 and 7, whereas triamcinolone acetonide 40 mg did not significantly differ from control; no combination group was tested.

entities.name: PMID:35955918
observations: In rat Achilles tendon cells and explant outgrowth, lidocaine at 0.5–1.5 mg/mL for 24 hours reduced proliferation and collagen I/III expression and increased MMP-2/MMP-9, without significantly increasing apoptosis; triamcinolone acetonide was not tested.

entities.name: PMID:25477418
observations: In human rotator-cuff-derived cells, triamcinolone acetonide at 0.1 or 1.0 mg/mL reduced viability and increased apoptosis/caspases at day 7; low-dose effects recovered by day 21, whereas 1.0 mg/mL caused persistent injury and repeated dosing prevented recovery. Lidocaine was not tested.

entities.name: PMID:27965219
observations: In IL-1β-stimulated human rotator-cuff-derived cells, triamcinolone acetonide at 0.1 mg/mL reduced viability and altered morphology; 10% platelet-rich plasma prevented these effects. Lidocaine was not tested.

entities.name: TA-lidocaine potentiation
observations: The strongest available evidence supports potentiation: in one direct rat-tenocyte study, triamcinolone acetonide plus 1% lidocaine was more harmful than either agent alone. The result is limited by a single direct study and unavailable TA dose/exposure duration in the retrieved record.
